original_test_intent: Verify the four temperature records represented by `TEMP_HIB_PEX1 ~4`—presumptively PEX PCIe switch/expander devices 1 through 4 on the Host Interface Board—are individually readable in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading with correct device identity, value, units, status and supported thresholds for the platform specification.
original_method: Confirm HIB and PEX terminology, resolve four stable sensor records, bind every PEX index to the exact HIB assembly location, switch device/part and PCIe-fabric plus BMC management path, then compare complete passive raw/UI fields with per-device limits under recorded fabric/load and airflow. Preserve logs, PCIe state and hardware configuration.
manual_activity: The platform owner confirms HIB/PEX semantics, identifies all four physical switch/expander devices and their BMC/fabric mapping, and provides per-device acceptance. Automation can collect the four records and UI rows separately; a human resolves chip/index/topology ambiguity and owns the verdict. No PCIe stress, reset or board service is authorized.
required_inputs: Exact chassis/HIB PN and revision, BMC/BIOS/PEX firmware plus Project definitions of HIB and PEX1-4
Per-index physical ASIC location, vendor/device ID or part/revision and PCIe upstream/downstream topology
BMC management source for each temperature, including controller, bus, mux, device address and exact die/board temperature field
Stable SDR name/number/type/entity/instance and Dashboard/Server Health row for each PEX1-4 sensor
Per-device units, scaling/rounding, tolerance, threshold capability/values/hysteresis, health, freshness and absent/unavailable semantics
Recorded PCIe traffic/link/power state, system load, fan mode/speeds, HIB airflow and any approved vendor/host telemetry correlation
Validated ipmitool/API/browser versions, protected authentication and pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or manual method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, kernel or PCIe logs; AER, link, switch, thermal and BMC history is relevant evidence.
Do not issue `sensor get 'TEMP_HIB_PEX1 ~4'` unless the vendor documents that literal record. Enumerate and query PEX1 through PEX4 separately with individual return/status evidence.

Do not infer that PEX indices are chassis slots. Bind each index to a physical HIB ASIC, device ID and fabric topology; downstream slots or cards are related context, not the sensor identity by default.

Treat I2C/I3C/management access as BMC/platform scope. Require controller/bus/mux/address and approved read-only path; a host PCIe enumeration or chip utility alone does not prove the BMC temperature field.

Do not generate PCIe traffic, reset/retrain a switch, change link settings, remove/reseat HIB or cards, alter fans or thresholds, or flash PEX firmware. Record existing fabric/load/cooling state only.

Do not truncate inventory, expose passwords using `-P`, assume cipher 17 or execute the unavailable Script. Stop without automatic retry on missing/duplicate/swapped devices, stale values or raw/UI/topology disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, HIB/PEX definitions, four-device physical/fabric/management topology, client and Script; build an expected device matrix before collection.
Retrieve PEX1-PEX4 independently with complete SDR identity, value, units, supported thresholds, status and timestamp; capture each unchanged Dashboard and Server Health row.
Correlate every record with physical ASIC/device ID and BMC bus/address plus recorded PCIe link/traffic/power and HIB cooling state; use vendor/host telemetry only if field equivalence is approved.
Preserve raw/redacted evidence and logs; perform no clear, PCIe load/link/reset/service, fan/threshold/firmware change, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Confirm HIB/PEX semantics and approve the four-ASIC physical, PCIe-fabric and BMC management-source map.
Provide per-device thermal thresholds, tolerance, status, freshness and any vendor telemetry equivalence, and approve the collection tool/Script.
Review PEX1 through PEX4 independently and issue the formal verdict without treating downstream slot/card evidence or one device as coverage for another.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Likely unfit because the spaced tilde expression is human range notation, not a guaranteed IPMI record, and one output cannot prove four PEX devices. It also omits HIB ASIC/fabric/bus/UI/spec mapping, truncates fallback data, exposes credentials and assumes cipher support.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate complete sensors, confirm the four HIB PEX device identities and BMC telemetry paths, resolve each vendor-supported record and retrieve it through protected read-only access, then correlate four UI rows with the approved ASIC/fabric matrix.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TEMP_HIB_PEX1 ~4, Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading, readability/specification Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek commands and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review expands the range without editing Master or exercising the PCIe fabric.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a four-row matrix keyed by HIB PEX ASIC identity and stable BMC sensor, documenting physical location, part/device ID, fabric topology and management bus/source, then compare complete raw/API and UI fields with per-device limits under a recorded passive fabric/cooling state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact HIB revision, PEX device/fabric population and BMC/SDR/WebUI build documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/HIB, BIOS/BMC/SDR/WebUI, PEX silicon/firmware, downstream population, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: HIB schematic/layout and PEX index map, PCIe fabric topology, BMC management-bus/sensor definition, PEX thermal limits, WebUI schema and Project configuration specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves range syntax into four physical ASIC-bound records, corrects slot-centric ambiguity and adds management-source/fabric evidence while preserving passive display coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Static PEX temperatures do not validate PCIe traffic thermal response, switch functionality, links, AER, throttling, reset/retrain, firmware or alarm/protection behavior; downstream slot/card temperatures are separate coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: HIB/PEX ASIC/fabric/bus map, per-device acceptance, load/cooling timing rules, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: PEX numbering can differ among schematic, BMC and PCIe enumeration; readings may be die or board sensors; UI polling can lag, and device absence depends on HIB variant.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM or vendor/host PEX telemetry as an approved alternative/corroboration only while preserving the original ipmitool method, recording interface/version/field and reason, obtaining engineer approval and proving equivalent separate PEX1-4 identity, value, threshold, status and freshness coverage. Downstream card or generic bridge temperature is not automatically equivalent.
expected_evidence: Chassis/HIB PN/revision, BMC/BIOS/PEX firmware and four-row PEX ASIC physical location, part/device ID and PCIe fabric topology matrix
BMC controller/bus/mux/address and exact temperature-field source for each PEX1-4 record
Complete separate raw records with stable IDs, values, units, threshold capabilities/values, status and timestamps
Separate redacted Dashboard and Server Health evidence mapped to the same four physical ASICs
Per-device Project/vendor specification plus recorded PCIe link/traffic/power and fan/HIB airflow state with tolerance/update-lag and any approved equivalent telemetry

Explicit missing/duplicate/swapped/stale/divergent disposition, pinned Script/tool security evidence, no-clear/no-load/no-reset/no-service/no-retry proof, final PCIe/BMC health and engineer-owned four-device verdict

Topology and sensor-source details are readiness inputs, not conflicting purposes.

review_improvement: Prevents a failed range query, downstream slot/card evidence or host enumeration from being presented as four HIB PEX device temperatures, and prevents service-impacting PCIe actions from being added to a passive display case.
independent_technical_reasoning: On a Host Interface Board, PEX commonly labels PCIe switch/expander devices, not physical slots themselves. Each index therefore needs a board location, device identity and fabric mapping, plus the BMC management source for the temperature. A host topology view can corroborate identity but not replace the BMC field; the source authorizes only passive readback, not traffic or reset testing.
